newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Apr 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong newspaper headlines-Apr 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- The marathon hostage crisis in Lima was resolved when Peruvian troops stormed the Japanese embassy. All but one of the 72 hostages were brought out alive and all 14 Marxist rebels were killed.
-- WEN WEI PO -- China and Russia signed a joint declaration announcing that the "Cold War mentality" must be dropped and urging the use of peaceful methods to resolve disputes between countries.
-- During his meeting with Russian leaders, Chinese President Jiang Zemin stressed that there was no doubt Hong Kong would have a brighter future after it returned to China.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Koo's Group, a Taiwan conglomerate, will set up the first Taiwanese overseas investment bank in Hong Kong. China Securities, the group's securities unit, planned to take a 15 percent stake in the new company.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- A row erupted between the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong and its Taiwan counterpart after the controversial launch in the territory of two call warrants linked to Taipei's benchmark index.
-- In a report, the International Monetary Fund proclaimed that China had achieved its much sought-after economic soft landing and forecast favourable conditions for the future.
